Type-level characteristics:
- q3/q1 ratio: 250 (unit "R" — ratio). Actually "R" here is ratio designation. unit_symbol: "R" or null. I'll use null or "R". Hmm. Let me use unit_symbol: null since it's dimensionless ratio... Actually the table says unit "R". I'll put "R".
- q2/q1 ratio: 1.6
- connection: "flange" (mm in unit column but value "flange" — it's a string; keep value "flange", unit null)
- installation_orientation: "H/V"
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C, temperature_class: "T50"
- maximum_admissible_pressure_map: 16 bar
- pressure_loss: 0.16 bar? Wait: "Pressure loss class Δp: bar / - : 0,16 / Δp 16". So pressure loss value 0.16 bar, pressure loss class "Δp16". Hmm, actually pressure loss class Δp16 corresponds to 0.16 bar? Typically Δp class... In water meters, pressure-loss classes are Δp63, Δp40, Δp25, Δp16, Δp10, Δp6.3, where Δp16 means max pressure loss of 0.16 bar (16 kPa? actually 0.16 bar = 16 kPa). So record:
  - pressure_loss_class: "Δp16" — but I shouldn't use LaTeX or subscript... "Δp 16" fine as "Δp16". Canonical label pressure_loss_class.
  - maximum_pressure_loss: 0.16 bar.
- mpe_upper_flowrates_range: ±2% for Q2 ≤ Q ≤ Q4 at temperature ≤30°C, ±3% at >30°C. This is a config-level characteristic (temperature condition). Note the text says "± 2 (at Ø ≤ 30°C) / ± 3 (at Ø>30°C)" — "Ø" is likely OCR for "θ" (temperature). So config_level:
  - attribute: mpe_upper_flowrates_range_q2_to_q4, axis: water_temperature, values: [{condition: "θ ≤ 30°C", value: 2, unit_symbol: "%"}, {condition: "θ > 30°C", value: 3, unit_symbol: "%"}]. Note the ± means symmetric. Value could be "±2"? Keep numeric 2 with note? Hmm. I'll put value 2 and mention... Actually the MPE is ±2%. I could keep value as 2 with unit "%". Maybe include "±" in value as string "±2"? Rule says numbers not strings. But "±2" isn't a number. I think value: 2, unit "%" is fine; maybe label it maximum permissible error. I could add "mpe_upper_flowrates_range" attribute. Keep value: 2 (the ± implied). Hmm, safer: value: {min: -2, max: 2}? That's over-interpretation. I'll use value: 2, unit_symbol: "%" — perhaps add note in condition. Actually, to preserve the ±, I could keep the label "mpe_upper_flowrates_range" and value 2. Fine.
- mpe_lower_flowrates_range: 5% (±5).
- capacity_of_calculator: 9999999.99 m³ (decimal comma fixed). Value 9999999.99.
- capacity_of_calculator_high_resolution: 999.999999 m³
- scale_interval: 0.01 m³
- scale_interval_high_resolution: 0.000001 L (that's 1 mL; keep as is)
- accuracy_class: "2" — accuracy class 2. Numeric 2.
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class: -55 to +85 °C. Note this seems odd (climatic class usually -25/+55 for O; but whatever). value {min:-55, max:85}, unit °C.
- electromagnetic_class: "E1"
- environmental_conditions_class: "B / O" (climatic and mechanical according to EN ISO 4064-1/OIML R 49-1). Value "B / O". Hmm — actually "B" is open field class, "O"? Keep as string "B / O".
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U5D3"
- battery: "non-replaceable li-battery 3,6 V, life time 10 years" → battery_voltage: 3.6 V; battery_type: "non-replaceable lithium"; battery_lifetime: 10 years.
- display: 9 digits LCD; indication range 999.999999 m³ to 9999999.99 m³.
- software_version: "20.5.P.7", checksum: "1202", display form "20.5.P.71202".
- reverse flow: not designed to measure reverse flow.
- communication: M-Bus default; options RS485/MODBUS, pulse, optical isolated, BACnet/MSTP, Radio, GSM.

Components: flow sensor, calculator and indication device — essential parts. The cert names flow sensor and calculator+indication as essential parts. I could add components entries:
- role: "flow sensor", description of body...
- role: "calculator and indication device", ...
The components schema: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. There aren't type designations for these. Characteristics could include details. Maybe keep simple: role and characteristics with the listed items? Might be noise. The schema says include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The cert does name "Flow sensor" and "Calculator and indication device" as essential parts. I'll include them with brief characteristics (as strings? characteristics{} free-form). I'll put characteristics with e.g. {"housing": "iron cylindrical body with inlet and outlet firmly connected with the plastic housing for the calculator"} etc. Keep minimal.
